name: Implementation independence is preserved across backend choices

input.fixture_ref: Run an identity-sensitive program through interpreter, JIT, and optimized representations and compare public values, diagnostics, and stable identities.

applicability.reason: Genuinely blocked on a second backend, verified rather than assumed. A DIFFERENTIAL row asserts that the interpreter and the JIT agree, which is only meaningful when both exist: with one backend any such comparison is self-agreement and proves nothing. The workspace has seven crates - iris-abi, iris-conformance, iris-eval, iris-lexer, iris-parser, iris-runtime, iris-syntax - and no JIT or AOT crate, feature or Cargo entry anywhere. This is not a missing surface that could be added alongside the others; it waits on the VM the owner has already scheduled separately.

expect.status: All backend choices preserve identical observable Iris behavior and public stable identities.
